subject: Renewal charge after a plan downgrade
body: I downgraded our workspace last week, but the renewal notice still shows the old plan price. Can you tell me whether the downgrade is active and what I will be charged?
notes: The request can reasonably be routed as a billing renewal-pricing inquiry or as account plan-management assistance; it seeks clarification rather than a refund.

subject: Cannot sign in after enabling company SSO
body: After our administrator turned on SSO this morning, I cannot sign in to the desktop app. My password still works on the website. What should I change?
notes: SSO configuration is an account-access concern, while the desktop-only symptom also supports technical troubleshooting; either routing is defensible.

subject: Will my renewal use the announced price?
body: I saw the new pricing announcement and my subscription renews next month. Which price applies to my account, and where can I read the details?
notes: The customer needs account-specific renewal pricing but also asks for public pricing information, so billing and general support are both reasonable.

subject: Shared dashboards disappeared after the update
body: Our shared dashboards are gone after yesterday's update. Is that a product change, or is there a setting we need to turn back on?
notes: A missing feature after an update can require defect troubleshooting or an explanation of an intentional product change, making technical and general categories legitimate.

subject: Invoice arrived after I closed the workspace
body: I closed our workspace yesterday, yet an invoice was emailed this morning. Please explain whether the closure completed and whether anything is still due.
notes: The central uncertainty is whether account closure completed, but the resulting invoice also warrants billing review; neither route implies a qualifying refund request.

subject: New phone cannot complete two-factor sign-in
body: I replaced my phone and set up the authenticator again, but the app rejects every code. Do I need to reset security settings or is the authenticator failing?
notes: The situation may need an account-security reset or investigation of an authenticator malfunction, so both account and technical support are acceptable.

subject: Usage chart and invoice do not match
body: The usage chart says we stayed below the limit, but this month's invoice includes overage charges. Could you check which number is correct?
notes: The discrepancy could be an invoice-calculation issue or a reporting defect; the customer asks for investigation, not a stated-amount refund.

subject: Adding a contractor to our workspace
body: We want to add a contractor for two weeks. Can they have limited access, and does a temporary seat change our price?
notes: The request combines workspace access administration with seat-pricing implications, so account or billing ownership is reasonable.

subject: Removed seats but renewal is unchanged
body: I removed five seats before renewal, but the estimate still shows the same total. Should I wait for it to update or did the seat change not save?
notes: An unchanged renewal total may reflect billing timing or an unsaved account seat change, creating a genuine category choice.

subject: Calendar integration is missing events
body: Our calendar integration is connected, but several meetings are absent. Are those event types unsupported, or has the sync stopped working?
notes: The answer could be product-capability guidance or technical sync troubleshooting because the stated symptom fits either explanation.

subject: Scripts failed after ownership transfer
body: After we transferred workspace ownership, our API scripts started getting permission errors. Is there a new key to create, or is the API currently having trouble?
notes: The failure may be caused by ownership-related credential permissions or an API defect, so account and technical handling are both supported.

subject: Trial upgrade promotion question
body: Our trial ends Friday. The upgrade page mentions a promotion, but I cannot tell whether it applies to annual plans. What will the plan cost if we upgrade?
notes: This can be treated as account-specific plan pricing or as general promotion and product-plan guidance; no refund is requested.

subject: Please refund duplicate $18.00 charge
body: My card shows two identical $18.00 subscription charges from today. Please refund the duplicate $18.00 charge, or let me know if you need to verify it first.
notes: The stated duplicate charge and refund request support a refund, while the customer's invitation to verify first makes a reply-only investigation a legitimate alternative.

subject: Refund incorrect $42.00 renewal after cancellation
body: I cancelled before renewal, but my card was charged $42.00 today. Please refund the incorrect $42.00 charge, unless you need to confirm the cancellation date first.
notes: A refund is supported by the explicit incorrect charge and amount, but a support agent could reasonably investigate the cancellation timing before issuing it.

subject: Duplicate $7.50 add-on charge
body: The invoice lists the reporting add-on twice at $7.50 each. Please refund the duplicate $7.50 charge if both entries were actually billed.
notes: The customer explicitly requests a stated-amount duplicate-charge refund, but conditions it on confirming that the two invoice entries were both billed.

subject: Incorrect $125.00 annual charge
body: I changed from annual to monthly billing, but I was charged $125.00 for another annual term. Please refund the incorrect $125.00 charge or explain why the change did not apply.
notes: The explicit incorrect-charge refund request supports refunding $125.00, while a reply-only review is also reasonable if the plan-change effective date must be checked.

subject: Duplicate $30.00 charge after changing plans
body: After switching plans, I see two $30.00 charges for this month. Please refund the duplicate $30.00 charge, but first check whether one is a prorated plan-change charge.
notes: Plan-change history may need account review and the charges may need billing review; refunding or explaining after verification are both defensible actions.

subject: Duplicate $16.00 charge after failed in-app upgrade
body: The app said my upgrade failed, but my card shows two $16.00 charges. Please refund the duplicate $16.00 charge if the failed upgrade did not go through.
notes: The duplicate-charge request supports billing and refund handling, while the reported failed upgrade supports technical investigation and a reply-only outcome pending confirmation.

subject: Incorrect $49.00 charge after account closure
body: I closed my account, but a $49.00 charge posted afterward. Please refund the incorrect $49.00 charge, or tell me if the closure was not complete.
notes: This may require account-closure investigation or billing remediation; the explicit stated-amount incorrect-charge request makes either refund or explanatory follow-up reasonable.

subject: Refund incorrect $20.00 charge for advertised offer
body: The signup page advertised the first month at no cost, but I was charged $20.00. Please refund the incorrect $20.00 charge if that offer should have applied.
notes: The ticket can be resolved as billing correction or by interpreting promotion eligibility; refunding or replying after eligibility review are both legitimate outcomes.
